comments.note: readJsonFile in src/storage/json-storage.ts calls fs.existsSync() then fs.readFileSync() — two syscalls. A single try/catch around readFileSync checking err.code === 'ENOENT' would be more idiomatic Node.js and avoids a TOCTOU race (another process could delete the file between the exist-check and the read). Low-risk for this tool but worth noting.

ensureDirectory does not guard against the case where dirPath already exists as a file rather than a directory. mkdirSync({ recursive: true }) will throw ENOTDIR in that scenario. For a config/storage tool this is unlikely, but a clearer error message would help diagnostics.

comments.note: Applied Fix-Forward to readJsonFile: removed the fs.existsSync() pre-check and restructured to a single try/catch around fs.readFileSync(). The ENOENT branch preserves the original 'File not found' message; all other I/O errors go through the 'Failed to read file' branch. This eliminates the TOCTOU race (file deleted between existsSync and readFileSync emitted a raw ENOENT instead of the descriptive message) and removes a redundant syscall. All error messages are identical from the caller's perspective. Build passes.

ensureDirectory does not guard the case where dirPath already exists as a regular file — mkdirSync throws ENOTDIR in that scenario. The error is opaque. For a dev-tool this is an unlikely edge case; the current behavior is acceptable but a stat-check and clear diagnostic message would help debugging. Deferred — low impact.
